basis.text: On 20 November 2023 a dance permit from the Entertainment Commission was needed to conduct a dance, unless the location held a valid Place of Entertainment permit.

A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). comparable_cases.why_comparable: Use decision (CUA) authorizing dancing at Badlands, an existing bar 30 meters away on 18th Street in the Castro NCD, approved in 1999. This is the closest comparable nightclub use in the district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Dancing in a bar requires a CUA in the Castro NCD. The Commission approved dancing at an existing bar on this block, establishing that nightclub uses are permissible with conditional use authorization even in this saturated corridor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Use decision (CUA) approving a Place of Entertainment permit as accessory to an established bar (The Edge) 68 meters away on 18th Street in the Castro NCD, decided in 2012. This is a bar adding live entertainment.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a POE for an existing bar on this block, confirming that entertainment uses accessory to bars are approvable with a CUA in the Castro NCD despite the corridor's density.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Use decision (CUA) at the subject property itself (4109-4111 18th / 500 Castro) modifying a prior CUA to limit live entertainment hours to midnight in a restaurant/bar, approved in 1998. This modified the 1996 approval at this same site.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: At this exact parcel, the Commission previously approved live entertainment in a restaurant/bar but conditioned entertainment to end at midnight (not 2 a.m.), suggesting sensitivity to late-night impacts at 500 Castro even with prior entertainment authorization.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Use decision (CUA) at the subject property (4109-4111 18th / 500 Castro) originally approving live entertainment in the Castro NCD in 1996. This was the first entertainment authorization at this parcel.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved live entertainment at this site in 1996, establishing precedent for entertainment use at 500 Castro, but the subsequent 1998 amendment limiting hours to midnight signals the Commission may restrict late-night entertainment at this location.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Use decision (miscellaneous permit) at the subject property (500 Castro / 4109-4111 18th) denied in 1996 for lack of conditional use authorization. This denial predated the successful CUA filing by three months.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning denied a place of entertainment permit at this exact parcel in 1996 because no CUA had been obtained, confirming that entertainment and dancing are not permitted by right and require Commission approval at 500 Castro.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Use decision (CUA) denied in 1994 for extended hours of operation at an existing bar 98 meters away at 465-469 Castro Street in the Castro NCD. This is the only outright denial among the nearby bar/entertainment cases.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission denied extended operating hours for a bar in the Castro NCD in 1994, demonstrating that late-night operations are not automatically granted and that the Commission will deny bar-use requests it finds inappropriate for the corridor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral (miscellaneous permit) at 4146 18th Street (77m away) in 2005 approving a bar as a nonconforming use but explicitly stating dancing is not permitted without a CUA. This is a comparable bar location on the same block.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a bar with recorded music and games but explicitly prohibited dancing without a CUA, reinforcing that dancing is not permitted as an ancillary activity in Castro NCD bars and requires separate conditional use authorization.

comparable_cases.address: 4146 - 4150 18TH ST STREET LEV, SAN FRANCISCO, CA 94114
comparable_cases.why_comparable: Use decision (miscellaneous permit) at 4146-4150 18th Street (77m away) in 2008 approving a bar with recorded music but stating 'DANCING IS NOT PERMITTED' without a CUA. Same location as MB0500058, reiterating the prohibition.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Three years after the prior decision at this same bar, Planning again approved recorded music and games but prohibited dancing without a CUA, confirming the consistent policy that dancing requires conditional use authorization in the Castro NCD.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral (miscellaneous permit) at 4067 18th Street (76m away) in 2011 recommending approval of a POE for an existing bar under Planning Code § 715.48, which allows existing bars to obtain POE permits without additional CU if they demonstrate regular entertainment operation.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a POE for an existing bar under the § 715.48 exemption, which allows bars that have been regularly operating as entertainment venues to get POE permits without a new CUA. This pathway does not apply to new bars or changes of use like this concept.

Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effective date of the Motion. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construc t the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period. (standard)

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new ap plication for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pursuit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay. (standard)

Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. MONITORING - AFTER ENTITLEMENT (standard)

Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning Code Section 176 or Section 176.1. The Planning Department may also refer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction. (standard)

Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commer cial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such comp laints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. OPERATION (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (A): The business operator shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Street and Sidewalk Maintena nce Standards. In addition, the operator shall be responsible for daily monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours, in accordance with Article 1, Section 34 of the San Francisco Police Code. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (B): When located within an enclosed space, the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed-source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (C): While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents an d passersby, appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (D): Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be cont ained and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Department of Public Works. Works at 415-554-.5810, http://sfdpw.org. (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups for the area with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liaison. (standard)

Odor Control Unit: In order to ensure any significant noxious or offensive odors are prevented from escaping the premises once the project is operational, the building permit application to implement the project shall include air cleaning or odor control equipment details and manufacturer specifications on the plans if applicable as determined by the project planner. Odor control ducting shall not be applied to the primary façade of the building. For information about compliance, contact the Case Planner, Planning Department at 415-558-6378, (standard)

timeline_cost.notes: The day and cost ranges cover the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000), Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800), health permit to operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000 for FY2026–27), and building permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000). The ranges are times to approval, not to denial or withdrawal. The CUA is the long pole (6–10 months including pre-application, environmental review, neighborhood notice and hearing scheduling). The cost does not include the ABC license: a Type 42 beer/wine bar is approximately $1,000–$1,600 in ABC fees and takes 60–150 days; a Type 48 full-liquor bar is typically purchased for $100,000–$450,000 (license purchase price plus transfer fees) and takes 90–240 days including escrow. Undue concentration in the census tract (46 ABC licenses within 1,000 ft) may add 1–3 months if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required. The figures do not include soft costs (architect, acoustic consultant, legal, broker), construction (tenant improvements to merge storefronts, soundproofing, ADA, bar build-out), or pre-opening operating expenses during the entitlement period.

records_summary: The records show 500 Castro Street sits in the Castro Street NCD where a bar use is conditional and requires a CUA; the pathway confirms this is a change of use from an existing restaurant (an active Type 47 license is on file). The site history reveals a long-running restaurant/bar at this address (Harvey's), with two CUAs approved in the late 1990s for live entertainment at the same parcel (1996.576C and 1998.034C, which amended entertainment hours to midnight). The block is saturated: 38 food and drink businesses within 500 feet, including 12 bars, and 28 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet (46 within 1,000 feet)—a density that flags undue concentration. Only two dated use decisions for comparable concepts were found nearby in the last ten years, both approved, but the count is too small to show a rate. The nearest comparable precedent is a 1999 CUA approving dancing at Badlands (30m away), and several bars on the block have POE permits for live entertainment, most with conditions limiting hours.
data_gaps: No conditions text extracted for the two 1990s CUAs at this parcel (1996.576C, 1998.034C); hearing transcripts and Motion text would show what hours, soundproofing, or capacity limits were imposed

No building permit or DBI records are included, so whether the existing space has adequate egress, ADA compliance, or a certificate of occupancy for assembly use is unknown
Entertainment Commission POE conditions (soundproofing, security plan, neighbor outreach) are not extracted for the comparable bars nearby
